back: A voluntary association of independent states, mostly former British colonies, sharing values such as democracy and development.
Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, normally every two years.

front: What did the London Declaration (1949) allow?
back: Republics, such as India, to remain Commonwealth members, with the monarch as Head of the Commonwealth.

front: What was decided at the Lusaka CHOGM (1979)?
back: That Britain should call an all-party conference on Rhodesia, which became the Lancaster House Conference.
A Commonwealth commitment to democracy, human rights and good governance, made at the CHOGM in Harare.

front: When did Zimbabwe leave the Commonwealth?

back: Bandung (1955): Asian-African conference; Belgrade (1961): first summit of the Non-Aligned Movement.

front: What happened at the NAM summit in Harare (1986)?
back: Mugabe became NAM chairman and the AFRICA Fund was set up to help the Frontline States.
